questions.prompt: What are we told about torching?

options.text: It sheltered the battens from the weather, so the timber under old roofs usually stayed sound.
It was what held the unnailed courses of tiles in place once they had been hung.
It made the loft weathertight the year round, whatever the weather drove against the roof.
It held the wet it took up against the battens, and the wood rotted there.
